Yes, gastric cancer is different in Korea and the United States in terms of incidence, prevalence, and characteristics. 

Korea has one of the highest incidence rates of gastric cancer worldwide, with a significantly higher rate compared to the United States. This is largely due to differences in diet, lifestyle, and genetic factors, as well as the high prevalence of Helicobacter pylori infection in Korea.

In Korea, gastric cancer tends to occur at a younger age, and the disease is often more aggressive. In contrast, gastric cancer in the United States is relatively rare and often diagnosed at an older age.

Additionally, the types of gastric cancer and the molecular characteristics of the disease also differ between the two countries. For example, diffuse-type gastric cancer is more common in the United States, while intestinal-type gastric cancer is more prevalent in Korea.

These differences highlight the importance of considering regional and ethnic variations in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of gastric cancer.
